summary: Full-extraction pass over 10 stored Cayman Islands documents (amending laws and regulations 2012-2025, consolidated regulations 2014 and 2018, the 2018 Transition Bill, the 2026 draft fee regulations and two 2026 press releases). They hold rules and fees, no counts of certificates. Added program terms for application, dependant, variation and duplicate fees, income and deposit alternatives, Sister Islands thresholds, the 250-a-year quota, validity periods, presence and shareholding rules, and new events.

program_terms.notes: Inserted by the Immigration (Amendment) Law 2012 (s.37D); valid_from is the gazette date (5 June 2012; assented 1 May 2012); commencement not stated in the text. Carried into s.50 of the Immigration (Transition) Bill 2018. Annual declaration of 90 days physical residence (s.37D(10)); failure to be resident 90 days is a ground for revocation (s.37D(11)(b)).

events.title: Cayman drops the personal net worth requirement for the Certificate of Direct Investment
events.description: The Immigration (Amendment) Law 2012 deleted from s.37A(1) the requirement that an applicant for a Certificate of Direct Investment have a personal net worth in a prescribed amount, and lowered a figure in the definition of "employment generating business" from fifty to thirty (the definition itself is not printed in the amending Law). Date is the gazette publication (assented 1 May 2012); commencement not stated.
events.location: PDF p. 6, s.10; PDF p. 3, s.2(a)
events.quote: by deleting the words “has a personal net worth in the prescribed amount and”

events.title: Cayman creates the Residency Certificate (Substantial Business Presence)
events.description: The Immigration (Amendment) Law 2012 inserted s.37D: residence for owners of at least 10% of, or senior managers in, an approved category of business with a substantial presence in the Islands, resident at least 90 days a year; a 6-month approval-in-principle certificate and a 25-year renewable certificate with the right to work in the business. Date is the gazette publication (passed 5 April 2012, assented 1 May 2012); commencement not stated.
events.quote: A NEW RESIDENCE CATEGORY FOR PERSONS WHO ESTABLISH A SUBSTANTIAL BUSINESS PRESENCE

events.title: First fees set for the business presence certificate
events.description: New Schedule 1 of the Immigration Regulations (made 3 Sept 2012) set CI$1,000 to apply for a Residency Certificate (Substantial Business Presence), CI$5,000 to issue it, CI$1,000 per dependant and CI$500 to vary it, plus an annual fee equal to the work permit fee for the holder's occupation. The same schedule lists CI$500/CI$20,000 for the 25-year independent-means certificate and CI$1,000/CI$20,000 for the Certificate of Direct Investment.
events.quote: Issue fee for Residency Certificate (Substantial Business Presence) 5,000

events.title: 25-year independent-means certificate: income or a CI$400,000 deposit
events.description: Besides doubling the investment (event e-45f0a5efc5), the 2017 regulations let applicants show either a continuous annual income (CI$120,000 Grand Cayman, CI$75,000 Sister Islands) or a deposit of at least CI$400,000 in assets with a CIMA-regulated local institution; before, the income was required in addition to the investment.
events.quote: maintains a minimum deposit in the account of at least four hundred thousand dollars in assets

events.title: Business presence certificate extended to Cayman Brac back-office firms
events.description: The 2017 regulations added to the approved categories any business operating from Cayman Brac providing HR, accounting, administrative, IT or other back-office support, kept exempted companies, and set the senior management test at an occupation with an annual work permit fee of CI$20,925 or more (CI$5,000 for the Cayman Brac back-office category).
events.quote: any business operating from within Cayman Brac providing Human Resource, Accounting, Administrative, IT, or other back- office support

events.title: Bill would let investor-residence holders prove financial standing through declarations by licensed professionals
events.description: The Memorandum of Objects and Reasons of the Immigration (Transition) Bill 2018 says holders of and applicants for the independent-means certificates, the Certificate of Direct Investment and the business presence certificate would show compliance with financial standing requirements by declarations issued by licensed financial institutions and professionals, removing those assessments from WORC, and that the business presence criteria would be revised to protect Caymanians' career advancement in financial services. The Bill also requires holders of the 25-year and permanent independent-means certificates to file an annual declaration (cl. 37(12)). Date is the Bill's publication.
events.location: pp. 2-3, Memorandum of Objects and Reasons
events.quote: to demonstrate compliance with prescribed financial standing requirements through submission of prescribed Declarations issued by financial institutions and financial professionals

events.title: Cayman gazettes immigration amendment: annual declarations and false-information offence for investor residents
events.description: Act 14 of 2025 (passed 12 Dec, assented 17 Dec, gazetted 18 Dec 2025) renames the Immigration (Transition) Act the Caymanian Protection Act; requires holders of the Certificate of Direct Investment and the business presence certificate to file annual declarations with a prescribed fee (failure is an offence and a ground for revocation); makes false information on financial standing or annual declarations an offence (fine CI$10,000 or one year); requires all permanent residents to pay prescribed fees for continued approval; and exempts existing holders of the independent-means permanent certificate (and their dependants) from the longer residence periods (twenty instead of fifteen years) for the grant of Caymanian status. Commencement by Cabinet order.
events.quote: a person who is the holder of a Certificate of Permanent Residence for Persons of Independent Means

events.title: Draft fees would raise the business presence certificate fee to CI$12,500 and add annual declaration filing fees
events.description: The consultation draft of the Immigration (Transition) (Fees) Regulations 2026 proposes CI$12,500 to issue a Residency Certificate (Substantial Business Presence) (from CI$5,000), CI$3,000 per dependant on issue and CI$3,000 per dependant per year for all investor certificates (from CI$1,000), CI$500 filing fees for the new annual declarations (25-year independent-means certificate, Certificate of Direct Investment, business presence certificate), and CI$100 for duplicate certificates (from CI$50). Application fees stay at CI$500 (independent means) and CI$1,000 (direct investment, business presence). Proposals only; adoption not confirmed. See also event e-a917a6edc3.
events.quote: Issue fee for Residency Certificate (Substantial 12,500 Business Presence)

events.title: Cayman drops 1 March 2026 as the start date of the new immigration law
events.description: Opening a two-week consultation (19 Feb-5 Mar 2026) on new immigration fees, the Ministry said 1 March 2026 was no longer the commencement date for the new legislation (the 2025 amending Act that changes the independent-means permanent certificate), with a new date to follow.
events.quote: 1 March 2026 is no longer the commencement date for the new legislation

events.title: Government sets 1 May 2026 for the immigration law changes
events.description: The Ministry and WORC confirmed that the immigration law changes (the 2025 amending Act, including the ten-year independent-means permanent certificate) take effect on Friday 1 May 2026, and that the revised fee regulations would start at the same time.
events.quote: the immigration law changes will take effect on Friday, 1 May 2026

gaps: No document in this batch gives counts of certificates issued, applications or revenue for any Cayman investor certificate.
The commencement date of the Immigration (Amendment) Law 2012 is not in the text; the gazette date is used.
Whether the 2026 draft fees were adopted is not confirmed by these documents.

ledger.contains: Gov.ky press release of 19 Feb 2026: public consultation (19 Feb-5 Mar 2026) on the draft Immigration (Transition) (Fees) Regulations 2026; fees not adjusted in more than 15 years; work permit fees unchanged but application fees tiered; lists the work-permit and 8-year permanent residence application fees to be raised (none of them investor certificates); says 1 March 2026 is no longer the commencement date of the new legislation. No investor-programme amounts or counts (the draft itself is cym-mcei-fees-regs-draft-2026). Added: one event (commencement date dropped).

Gov.ky press release of 27 Mar 2026: the immigration law changes take effect on Friday 1 May 2026; WORC systems, forms and training being readied; revised fee regulations to start at the same time; existing channels stay open. No numbers about the investor certificates. Added: one event (1 May 2026 start date).

Immigration (Amendment) Law 2012 (Law 2 of 2012), 15 pp.: Appeals Tribunal composition; s.34A permanent residence for persons of independent means (investment in developed real estate, quota set by the Governor and gazetted, no right to work, variation to work); s.36A revocation if investment not maintained; s.37A Certificate of Direct Investment loses the personal net worth requirement; "employment generating business" definition fifty -> thirty; s.37C specialist caregivers; s.37D Residency Certificate (Substantial Business Presence): 90 days a year, 10% shareholding or senior management, 6-month approval in principle, 25-year renewable certificate, dependent children to 24, annual declaration and revocation grounds; visitor's work visa, administrative fines register, sports fishing vessels, student visas (out of scope). Passed 5 Apr 2012, assented 1 May 2012, gazetted 5 Jun 2012. Added: 4 terms (SBP 90 days, 10%, 6 months, 25 years) and 2 events (CDI net worth requirement removed; SBP launch). Existing event e-e769dfb540 covers s.34A.

Immigration (Amendment) (No. 2) Regulations 2012, 86 pp.: a new Schedule 1 of fees (visas, business staffing plans, Caymanian status, permanent residence and RERC fees by earnings band, specialist caregivers, business visitors, temporary and annual work permits, and the occupation-by-occupation annual work permit fee list pp. 26-85, out of scope; Part 3 Cayman Enterprise City CI$1,230 flat fee, out of scope). In scope: fees for the 25-year independent-means certificate (CI$500 application, CI$20,000 issue, CI$1,000 dependant, CI$500 variation), the Certificate of Direct Investment (CI$1,000, CI$20,000, CI$1,000 per dependant, CI$500 variation, CI$1,000 per dependant annual plus work-permit-equivalent annual fee), the business presence certificate (CI$1,000, CI$5,000, CI$1,000 per dependant, CI$500 variation, annual work-permit-equivalent fee) and CI$50 duplicates (business presence, direct investment, permanent independent means). The schedule has no issue or application fee for the permanent independent-means certificate itself. Added: 13 terms and 1 event; the three issue fees were already recorded (t-e02df43ec4, t-00a8b87354, t-5d2f75c0da).

Immigration (Amendment) (No. 4) Regulations 2017, 5 pp.: reg 14 (25-year independent-means certificate): Grand Cayman CI$120,000 annual income or CI$400,000 deposit, plus CI$1m invested of which CI$500,000 in developed real estate; Sister Islands CI$75,000 income or CI$400,000 deposit, plus CI$500,000 of which CI$250,000 in real estate; definition of assets. Reg 14B: permanent certificate CI$2m (was CI$1.6m). Reg 14C: new business presence categories (hedge fund incubation; Cayman Brac back-office; exempted companies) and senior management thresholds (work permit fee CI$20,925, or CI$5,000 for the Cayman Brac category). Schedule 1: "per dependant" inserted and CI$1,000 per dependant p.a. fees for the three certificates. Made 17 May 2017, gazetted 26 May 2017. Added: 9 terms and 2 events; CI$1m and CI$2m terms and event e-45f0a5efc5 were already recorded.

Immigration Regulations (2014 Revision), 128 pp. Out of scope: work permit procedures, visas, points system for permanent residence (Schedule 2), business staffing plans, the occupation fee list (pp. 34-91) and forms for other certificates. In scope: reg 14 (25-year independent-means certificate: CI$120,000 income AND CI$500,000 invested of which CI$250,000 real estate on Grand Cayman; CI$75,000 and CI$250,000/CI$125,000 on the Sister Islands); reg 14A Certificate of Direct Investment CI$1m; reg 14B permanent certificate CI$1.6m and quota 250 a year; reg 14C business presence (physical premises, four full-time resident employees, approved categories, senior management at a CI$20,925 work permit fee); Schedule 1 fees for the three certificates and the permanent certificate (CI$500 application, CI$100,000 issue, CI$1,000 per dependant, CI$500 variation) and CI$50 duplicates; Form 3 (25-year certificate). Added: 10 terms; four terms from this source already existed (t-0684e733b5, t-4604d5c722, t-337f4426f1, t-aaf25e822e). Fees equal to the 2012 schedule are recorded once, from cym-imm-amend2-regs-2012.

Immigration Regulations (2018 Revision), 128 pp.: consolidation to February 2018 including the 2017 amendments. Investor provisions (reg 14, 14A, 14B incl. quota 250, 14C; Schedule 1 fees pp. 32-35; Form 3) are word-for-word the 2017 amended text and the 2014 fee amounts, already recorded from cym-imm-amend4-regs-2017, cym-imm-regs-2014rev and cym-imm-amend2-regs-2012; the notes of those terms say the 2018 revision is unchanged. Rest (work permits, visas, points system, occupation fees) out of scope. No new rows: nothing in it differs from the earlier sources.

Immigration (Transition) (Amendment and Validation) Act 2025 (Act 14 of 2025), 52 pp. In scope: definitions of developed real estate and paid-up amount (s.3); s.17 permanent independent-means certificate for ten years, renewable indefinitely, naturalisation possible one year after indefinite renewal, investment tested at application; s.14 (new s.37(12)) annual declaration for holders of s.41/42 certificates; s.18 and s.21 annual declarations for direct investment and business presence holders; s.13 prescribed fees for continued permanent residence; s.36 offences for false financial standing information or declarations (CI$10,000 or 1 year); s.37 transitional rules (pending applications under the old law; existing independent-means permanent holders exempt from the 15->20 year status residence change). Out of scope: Caymanian status by marriage, civil servants' term limits, commercial farmhands, work permits, validation of fees and fines. Added: 6 terms (10-year validity, 1-year naturalisation wait, CI$10,000 penalty x4 programmes) and 1 event; event e-809a44287d already recorded s.17.

Consultation draft of the Immigration (Transition) (Fees) Regulations 2026, 89 pp.: refunds and exemptions; Schedule Part 1 general fees (Caymanian status, permanent residence by earnings band, RERC, investor certificates items 8-11, duplicates item 14, business visitors) and Part 2 work permit fees by occupation (pp. 16-89, out of scope). Investor items: 25-year certificate CI$500 application, CI$50,000 issue, CI$3,000 per dependant and per dependant per year, CI$500 declaration filing, CI$500 variation; permanent certificate CI$500, CI$200,000, CI$3,000, CI$3,000 p.a., CI$500 variation; direct investment CI$1,000, CI$50,000, CI$3,000, CI$3,000 p.a., CI$500 variation, CI$500 declaration; business presence CI$1,000, CI$12,500, CI$3,000, CI$3,000 p.a., CI$500 variation, CI$500 declaration; duplicates CI$100. These are proposals, so, as the dataset does for proposals, they are recorded as events (existing e-a917a6edc3 plus one new event covering the rest) and in the notes of the current terms, not as program terms.

Immigration (Transition) Bill 2018, 87 pp.: memorandum (WORC and Customs and Border Control from 1 Jan 2019; financial standing to be shown by declarations from licensed professionals for the investor certificates; business presence criteria to be revised); Parts on WORC, Boards, appeals (refusals of investor certificates appealable to the Caymanian Status and Permanent Residency Board), Caymanian status, permanent residence (s.37(12) annual declaration for s.41/42 holders), s.41-46 independent-means certificates (25 years, age 18, 30 days a year, quota gazetted by Cabinet, revocation), s.47-48 Certificate of Direct Investment (6-month approval in principle, 25 years, audited accounts in years 2 and 5, 90 days a year), s.50 business presence (same as 2012 Law), work permits and regulations (out of scope). The Bill sets no amounts (they are "prescribed"). Added: 5 terms and 1 event; event e-112d2118b5 already recorded.
